column1: # Running a machine's system activation is the operator's switch gesture: it changes what runs, as root, and on a
# seat it can reach tart:vm:factory-reset:apply, whose rm -rf destroys a guest's disks (its Incus DB included). The
# sessions have passwordless sudo here, so the deny hook is the only barrier. Columns, tab-separated: want
# (DENY|ALLOW), today (bad62b2a's hook, measured), cwd (- for /tmp/work), cmd. A case is loosened only with 🛡️'s review.
# The activation script itself, by every path a system profile reaches it.
# NixOS: the switch program inside a system closure.
# Behind a launcher, a shell or a prefix.
# Pointing the system profile at another closure is half of a switch.
# Setting the factory-reset variable at all, for any command.
# Already refused: the darwin-rebuild front door (kept so a rewrite keeps them).
# Reading an activation script, or listing a profile, changes nothing.
